A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository was found in the collected evidence. The GitHub URL https://github.com/gocardless/gc-mcp returned 404. A community repository exists but is unofficial and was excluded from tool evidence.
other_official_servers: The same-host root endpoint https://mcp.gocardless.com is the URL used in current official setup instructions; the input endpoint is https://mcp.gocardless.com/mcp. The available evidence does not establish whether their tool sets differ.
GoCardless documents a CLI/local MCP configuration path as well as remote hosted MCP access; the CLI is a separate access/setup route, not evidence of another hosted MCP endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: GoCardless terms say the CLI, MCP, MCP Data, and MCP Services are free of charge and reserve the right to charge in the future. No MCP-specific call fee or usage quota was found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Standard, Advanced, and Pro transaction plans and a Custom plan; the page gives per-transaction pricing rather than a standalone MCP subscription. Prices vary by transaction type, market, and plan.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Official pricing shows transaction fees for the linked payment service; the MCP terms separately state that MCP access is currently free and could be charged in the future. No MCP per-call charge, credits, or quota found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth is required. The user chooses permissions, including read-only or specific write access. Official setup says Team or Enterprise organization owners must first connect the connector. Users choose Sandbox or Live during sign-in and reconnect to switch environments. Blog states reauthentication every two weeks for read-write and monthly for read-only access.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: GoCardless controls OAuth and service availability; the account user chooses permissions and environment; organization owners control initial setup for Team or Enterprise plans.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read/write actions are described, but official tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were not published. Third-party catalogue descriptions identify read and write actions. 2. Official docs state money-moving actions need confirmation and recommend checking previews. Third-party descriptions specify confirmed=false preview then confirmed=true execution for create/cancel/update operations; enforcement by the server is not independently verified. 3. OAuth required. Metadata advertises authorization_code, PKCE S256, DCR, and token auth method none; scopes_supported is absent. Docs say users choose read-only or specific write permissions. Blog reports reauthentication every two weeks for read-write and monthly for read-only. 4. Sandbox and Live are selectable; docs say reconnect to switch. No documented URL toolset/filter or read-only mode parameter. 5. Official docs say sensitive customer data is masked. Blog names bank account numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers as masked PII. 6. No general rate/quota data found. Third-party tool descriptions state bulk caps: 10 mandate/payment cancellations and 25 payment/subscription creations; event history may exclude data older than 18 months. 7. No official schemas/code for validation behavior. Third-party descriptions state operation-specific state, schedule, scheme, and currency requirements. 8. No MCP call logging or telemetry details found. list_events is described as an account state-change event feed, not MCP audit logging. 9. Third-party tool submit_feedback asks for a 1–5 helpfulness rating when the user expresses satisfaction/dissatisfaction or requests feedback; this is not in an official tool list. No upsell response found. 10. Docs recommend client prompt guidance; no official server-delivered skills or initialize instructions found. Tool descriptions in third-party listings include behavioral rules. 11. No evidence that past agent behavior changes server outputs, tools, resources, or prompts. 12. Evidence indicates a hosted endpoint plus documented local CLI/MCP route; no documented hierarchy or sub-server routing. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent escape-hatch tool found in the reported tool list.

[THIRD-PARTY AgentDiscoverability.com, 2026-10-27] "If the user asks to cancel more than 10 mandates, do NOT call this tool multiple times to work around the cap."

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official machine-readable tool list or official total was found in the vendor docs, checked pages, or public code search. AgentDiscoverability.com reported 25 tools and supplied the names/descriptions used here; all 25 are labelled third-party because the vendor does not publish their machine names. Manufact reported 2 tools (integrate_with_gocardless, read_gocardless_resource); Composio reported 24 human-readable tools; mcp.so said its tool list was unavailable; Claude's connector page showed no tool list. The different catalogue counts are unresolved. No additional catalogue-only tools were added beyond the 25-name listing.

actions.description: Overview of GoCardless integration options; description directs a follow-up resource read.
Cancel a mandate with preview and confirmation; cancellation also cancels attached subscriptions and pending payments.
Cancel an eligible payment before bank submission, using a preview and confirmation flow.
Create a one-off payment against an existing mandate after preview and confirmation.
Create a single-use hosted Billing Request authorisation link.
Create a reusable Billing Request Template authorisation link.
Create recurring subscriptions against one or more mandates with preview and confirmation.
Retrieve one customer by ID; PII fields are partially masked.
Retrieve one Direct Debit mandate by ID.
Retrieve one payment by ID.
Retrieve one payout settlement by ID.
Retrieve one recurring subscription by ID.
Return the current sandbox or live environment and instructions for switching.
List customers, optionally filtered by creation date; PII fields are partially masked.
List resource state-change events for audit trails and webhook debugging; older than 18 months may be unavailable.
Search or filter mandates by status, customer, or scheme.
Search, filter, or count payments by status, customer, mandate, subscription, currency, or date range.
Search or filter payouts by status, currency, or date range.
Search or filter refunds by payment, mandate, or date range.
Search or filter recurring subscriptions by status, customer, or mandate.
Submit a one-to-five session helpfulness rating when the user expresses satisfaction or dissatisfaction, or requests feedback submission.
Update an active subscription's amount, name, payment reference, metadata, or retry setting with preview and confirmation.
Issue a refund; catalogue says refunds:write permission is required.
Retrieve one refund by ID; catalogue says refunds:read permission is required.
Fetch GoCardless API documentation, integration guides, how-to content, or code samples by URI.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or official verbatim tool definitions/initialize instructions; catalogue descriptions are not sufficient to compute the requested context token count.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The official docs describe integration guidance, payment page implementation, API endpoint information, webhooks, code samples, and account operations, but do not enumerate the complete MCP-versus-dashboard/API operation boundary. The third-party list lacks some tool schemas and parameters, so additional inaccessible operations cannot be established from this evidence. The vendor's API documentation and guides are available through the documented guidance capability; no REST-only parameters were used as MCP parameters.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official client guidance says: "For any prompt that mentions GoCardless, use the GoCardless MCP." It recommends being specific, naming the resource and amount, and checking a preview before approval. These are client/agent instructions; server enforcement is unverified. Official security guidance says to avoid sharing API keys with the LLM and test write actions in Sandbox.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Official docs state sensitive customer data is masked and money-moving actions need confirmation. The vendor blog specifies masking of bank account numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers and reports OAuth reauthentication intervals. Live terms require the user to protect MCP Data and prohibit its use to process personal data; they also say the AI service provider must not use data to train models and must delete it after incorporating it into output. These are contractual terms, not verified server-side controls.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes the MCP as providing integration guidance and live account data access, with selectable permissions from read-only to specific write actions. Terms state the CLI, MCP, MCP Data, and MCP Services are free of charge while reserving a right to charge in the future; service availability is not guaranteed uninterrupted.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth challenge and authorization metadata substantiate OAuth access, but no code or tool schemas were available to verify permission enforcement, masking, confirmation, deletion, or training restrictions in the server/client implementation. Confirmation guidance and tool-level two-step instructions are documentation/catalogue evidence; the endpoint's enforcement behavior is untested.

contradictions: Official setup docs use https://mcp.gocardless.com while the input endpoint and API Commons listing use https://mcp.gocardless.com/mcp; the available evidence does not establish whether these paths expose identical tools.

Tool-count catalogues conflict: AgentDiscoverability.com reports 25, Composio 24, Manufact 2, and mcp.so says the tool list is unavailable. The vendor does not publish a named official list to resolve the difference.

Official docs say sensitive customer data is masked generally; the vendor blog names bank account numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers. The specific fields/coverage cannot be checked against server code or schemas.
observations_for_research: Official docs combine developer documentation guidance and live account actions behind the same MCP offering.
The endpoint exposes OAuth metadata with DCR and PKCE but no advertised scopes_supported; vendor setup instead describes user-selected permission authorization.

Third-party tool descriptions convey detailed agent behavior, including previews, explicit confirmations, batch sequencing, and operation constraints, while the vendor's public docs do not publish machine tool names or schemas.
